title: Mapping murine transcription factor interactomes using affinity purification and ChIP-seq
author: Gabele, Cihan, et al.
materials: The following section briefly outlines how analyze the samples by LC-MS analysis. In general, any high-resolution, state-of-the-art LC-MS instrument platform can be used for LC-MS analysis. In the study by Gabele et al.,1 samples were analyzed on an Ultimate 3000 RSLCnano LC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to an Orbitrap Exploris 480 instrument platform (Thermo Fisher Scientific).36.Perform LC-MS analysis of the tryptic digests.a.Separate tryptic peptides by reverse-phase LC.Note: For peptide separation, we favor the use of commercial reverse-phase C18 HPLC columns with the following dimensions: 75 μm inner diameter (ID) x 25 cm length, particle size ≤ 1.8 μm (see key resources table). However, shorter columns and/or inner diameters of 150 μm can be used as well. Similarly, we favor a trap setup, where peptides are first loaded onto a PEPMAP100 C18 5 μm 0.3 × 5 mm trap column (Thermo Fisher Scientific) to extend the lifetime of the analytical column. Typically, we run 30–40 min gradients for the chromatographic separation of peptides, but shorter gradients should suffice as well.b.Analyze eluting peptides by MS.Note: For mass spectrometric analysis of eluting peptides, we favor data-independent acquisition (DIA) methods. We recommend the following settings on the Orbitrap Exploris 480 instrument platform: Spray voltage of 1.8 kV (may need to be adjusted depending on the emitter setup used), funnel RF level at 40, and heated capillary temperature at 275°C, full MS resolution set to 120,000 at m/z 200 and full MS automated gain control (AGC) target to 300% with a maximum injection time (IT) of 20 ms. Set mass range to m/z 345 – 1,250. Acquire fragment ion spectra with an AGC target value of 1000%. We recommend to program around 20 windows with varying sizes (adjusted to precursor density) and an overlap of 0.5 Th at a resolution of 30,000. IT can be determined automatically (“auto mode”). Fix HCD collision energy was at 27%. Acquire all data in profile mode using positive polarity.Note: It is beyond the scope of this protocol to exhaustively review all options for the LC-MS/MS analyses as these depend on the instrument platforms available. Here, we describe our preferences and provide some comments on the settings.

steps.title: Harvest and wash primary T cells
steps.instruction: Collect in‑vitro differentiated Th17 cells, wash, count and adjust cell numbers for each pulldown (≈3 × 10⁷ cells per sample).

substeps.instruction: Resuspend cells and transfer to a 50 mL tube.
Wash the culture plate with pre‑warmed PBS, combine wash with cells.
Wash the collected cells twice with cold PBS (10 min, 630 × g, 4 °C) to remove medium.
Count cells and adjust numbers so that biotinylated and control samples contain equal cell counts (≈3 × 10⁷ cells per pulldown).

steps.title: Crosslink interacting proteins with DSP
steps.instruction: Crosslink proteins in suspension cells using 0.75 mM DSP, then quench with Tris.

substeps.instruction: Discard PBS after the last wash.
Resuspend cells in DSP working solution (0.75 mM; use 500 µL per 1 × 10⁷ cells; prepare a master mix for all samples).
Incubate at room temperature for 30 min, inverting the tube at regular intervals.
Add crosslinker‑stopping solution to a final concentration of 20 mM Tris (e.g., 10 µL per 500 µL DSP solution).
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min, inverting regularly.
Wash cells twice with cold PBS (10 min, 630 × g, 4 °C).

steps.title: Isolate cell nuclei
steps.instruction: Lyse cells gently, isolate and wash nuclei in hypotonic buffer with protease inhibitors.

substeps.instruction: Add 50× PIC stock to hypotonic buffer at 1:50 dilution to make 1× PIC‑supplemented hypotonic buffer (use 1 mL per 1 × 10⁷ cells).
Discard PBS after the last wash.
Resuspend cells in the 1× PIC‑hypotonic buffer.
Incubate on ice for 12 min (adjust incubation time for each cell type).
Add Igepal to a final concentration of 0.5 % (v/v) (add 10 % (v/v) Igepal and vortex 10 s).
Pellet nuclei (10 min, 850 × g, 4 °C).
Wash nuclei twice with 10 mL cold PBS (10 min, 850 × g, 4 °C).
Transfer nuclei to fresh 1.5 mL LoBind protein Eppendorf tubes, discard supernatant, and keep nuclei dry.
Pause point: store nuclei at –80 °C or proceed directly to immunoprecipitation.

steps.title: Lyse nuclei and prepare nuclear lysate
steps.instruction: Lyse nuclei in RIPA buffer with PIC, sonicate, and clarify lysate.

substeps.instruction: If nuclei were frozen, thaw gently on ice.
Add 30 µL RIPA buffer (supplemented with 1× PIC) to each nuclei pellet and mix gently.
Sonicate twice in a Bioruptor Plus (low power, 30 s ON/30 s OFF) for a total of 5 min at 4 °C, inverting and spinning down between cycles.
Centrifuge lysates 6 min at 14,850 × g, 4 °C.
Transfer supernatant (nuclear proteins) to a new 1.5 mL LoBind tube; keep on ice.
Optional: keep a small aliquot as input control for western blot.

steps.title: Prepare streptavidin magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Wash and equilibrate magnetic streptavidin beads for binding.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend magnetic streptavidin‑coated beads.
Aliquot 15 µL beads per sample into a 1.5 mL LoBind tube.
Place tube on a magnet, discard storage buffer.
Wash beads with RIPA buffer on a rotating shaker for 10 min at 21‑24 °C.
Spin briefly, place on magnet, discard supernatant.
Resuspend beads in 60 µL RIPA buffer containing 1× PIC.

steps.title: Bind nuclear lysate to beads
steps.instruction: Incubate lysate with prepared streptavidin beads overnight.

substeps.instruction: Add the resuspended beads to the nuclear lysate.
Rotate the mixture overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash and elute bound protein complexes
steps.instruction: Perform six sequential washes, then elute proteins from beads.

substeps.instruction: Spin briefly, place on magnet for ~2 min, discard supernatant.
Resuspend beads in 1 mL Wash Buffer I, rotate 10 min at 21‑24 °C.
Repeat Wash Buffer I two more times (total three washes with Buffer I).
Resuspend beads in 1 mL Wash Buffer II, rotate 10 min at 21‑24 °C.
Repeat Wash Buffer II two more times (total three washes with Buffer II; six washes overall).
Discard supernatant after the final wash.
Resuspend beads in 50 µL SDS‑biotin buffer.
Incubate 5 min at 95 °C while shaking at 350 U/min to elute proteins.
Place tubes on magnet for 2 min, transfer supernatant to a new 1.5 mL LoBind tube.
Optional: keep a small eluate aliquot for western blot.
Pause point: store eluates at –80 °C or proceed to proteolytic digestion.

steps.title: LC‑MS analysis of tryptic digests
steps.instruction: Separate peptides by nano‑LC and acquire data on an Orbitrap Exploris 480 using DIA settings.

substeps.instruction: Load tryptic peptides onto a C18 analytical column (75 µm ID × 25 cm, ≤1.8 µm particles) preceded by a PEPMAP100 C18 trap column (5 µm, 0.3 × 5 mm).
Run a 30–40 min gradient (shorter gradients are acceptable).
Set MS parameters: spray voltage 1.8 kV, funnel RF level 40, heated capillary 275 °C, full MS resolution 120,000 at m/z 200, AGC target 300 % with max injection time 20 ms, mass range m/z 345‑1250.
Acquire DIA data with ~20 windows (overlap 0.5 Th), resolution 30,000, AGC target 1000 %, HCD collision energy 27 %, profile mode, positive polarity.

steps.title: Annotate peaks with immune TF motifs
steps.instruction: Use TRANSFAC‑Match to annotate Bio‑ChIP‑seq peaks with immune‑specific transcription‑factor motifs.

substeps.instruction: Extract genomic sequences of peaks (e.g., mm10) and prepare a MATCH configuration file (e.g., th17_config.xml) that references the immune_cell_specific_modified.prf matrix file.
Run the MATCH algorithm: cd TRANSFAC/match/bin/; ./match.sh path/to/th17_config.xml (adjust path as needed).
Convert MATCH output to a structured CSV (parallelized on 40 cores or as available) and write to th17_combs.csv.
Count motif‑pair co‑occurrences per region: group by TF1 and TF2, summarize distinct peak IDs, sort descending, and write to th17_combs_pair_counts.csv.
